definitions.explanation: A rectangular block of clay hardened by drying or firing, used in building construction.

examples.japanese: {煉瓦|れんが}⟦{造|づく}り→造る：17751_tsukuru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{建物|たてもの}→建物：01458_tatemono⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{丈夫|じょうぶ}→丈夫：01156_joubu⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
⟦{赤|あか}い→赤い：00585_akai⟧{煉瓦|れんが}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{倉庫|そうこ}→倉庫：04044_souko⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{観光|かんこう}→観光：00173_kankou⟧⟦{名所|めいしょ}→名所：08164_meisho⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なっている→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: The red brick warehouse has become a tourist attraction.

examples.japanese: ⟦{庭|にわ}→庭：02239_niwa⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{煉瓦|れんが}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{花壇|かだん}→花壇：11075_kadan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}った→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: I made a flower bed with bricks in the garden.

notes:
USAGE: {煉瓦|れんが} can also be written as レンガ in katakana in modern usage.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {煉瓦|れんが}⟦{造|づく}り→造る：17751_tsukuru⟧ (brick construction)
- {煉瓦|れんが}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{積|つ}む→積む：02294_tsumu⟧ (to stack/lay bricks)
- ⟦{赤|あか}→赤：02842_aka⟧{煉瓦|れんが} (red brick)

COUNTER: ⟦{個|こ}→〜個：00645_ko⟧ or ⟦{枚|まい}→〜枚：00650_mai⟧

CULTURAL NOTE: Red brick (⟦{赤|あか}→赤：02842_aka⟧{煉瓦|れんが}) buildings from the Meiji era are often preserved as historical landmarks in Japan, particularly in Yokohama, Hakodate, and other port cities that were early to adopt Western architecture.
